video_title: Bitcoin Is Just Getting Started, Says Billion Dollar Investor
gist: Anson Funds co-founder/CIO Moaz Kassam explains his sentiment-driven playbook of entering themes early and exiting before peak hype, detailing ~$1B deployed into Bitcoin treasury companies (incl. a discounted Strive perpetual-preferred arb), skepticism of AI valuations and SPV-layered private AI deals, trading against LLM-summarized research reactions, and contrarian calls on Korean memory, CoreWeave, Moderna, small-cap long activism (Lionsgate) and SPACs at trust.

insights.claim: Anson Funds' core approach is not to avoid hype but to get in on a theme as it starts to percolate and exit before peak euphoria, judging crowd size and 'how loud the music is' rather than trying to ride to the ninth inning.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Take profits on crowded themes around the seventh inning; size exits to sentiment, not fundamentals alone.
insights.quote: it's make sure you're on the other side of the hype

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam argues post-COVID retail participation (GameStop, AMC era) means hyped names can run much further, longer and higher than expected, so short-side and exit timing require patience and prudent risk sizing.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Avoid aggressive shorts against retail-favored momentum names; size small and stay patient.
insights.quote: things can go up a lot faster and a lot longer and a lot higher than you think

insights.claim: Anson runs roughly US$2.5–3 billion but underwrites multiple billions of dollars of deals per year, profiting from issuance waves that follow every hype theme (autonomous driving, crypto, cannabis) because liquidity and correlated moves create deal flow.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Hot themes produce equity/convert issuance waves; deal underwriters capture discounted entries as the theme peaks.

insights.claim: Anson's typical holding period is weeks to months, with larger trades held longer; the fund prefers many 'singles and doubles' with a high batting average over home runs, with rare 2–4% single-day gains.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Frames the fund as a high-turnover sentiment trader rather than a long-term holder.

insights.claim: Anson's best single day was about $80 million from an arbitrage around the National Bank of Greece recapitalization.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Recap/restructuring arbitrages can produce outsized single-day payoffs.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam tells portfolio companies Anson is 'here for a good time, not a long time': it exits once things are good and the company no longer needs capital, then returns as a liquidity provider at the next hiccup.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Expect fast exits from PIPE/underwriting investors after a re-rate; their selling can cap post-deal rallies.
insights.quote: we're here for a good time, not a long time

insights.claim: Anson has grown AUM through returns rather than fundraising: it has made about $3 billion, takes in little new money, and has net redemptions every year because it does not market, deliberately staying small enough to have an edge.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Capacity discipline is a source of edge; small-cap specialists lose it when they grow.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam now believes Bitcoin has inherent value and is here to stay, having evolved from a purely deal-driven involvement because major institutions have adopted it and put it on their platforms.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Institutional adoption has shifted even deal-focused hedge funds toward structural Bitcoin belief.
insights.quote: now I believe Bitcoin has an inherent value and it's here to stay

insights.claim: Because early crypto companies listed in Toronto where few hedge funds operated, Anson was naturally exposed to names like Hive and was the original fund backing Mike Novogratz's Galaxy.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Canada's listing venues give local funds first-call access to new speculative sectors.

insights.claim: Anson deployed about $1 billion into Bitcoin treasury companies (DATs) over the last 18 months, scaling from $20–50 million checks, and concluded first-mover advantage is huge while late entrants get much worse deals.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Favor early, well-sponsored treasury companies; avoid the late wave of me-too DATs.
insights.quote: eventually we gave a billion dollars to uh you know treasury companies last in the last 18 months

insights.claim: With some 74 Bitcoin treasury companies coming to market, Moaz Kassam says the later and louder the music, the worse the deals, as too many players chase get-rich-quick structures.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Saturation in the DAT trade signals the end of the momentum phase for the category.

insights.claim: Most Bitcoin treasury companies now trade at big discounts to NAV, but activism to capture the discount is hampered by bad covenants that require paying management three to five years of forward earnings to remove them, eroding the discount.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Don't assume NAV-discount DATs are easy activist arbs; check management-removal covenants first.

insights.claim: Anson was a large buyer of Strive's SATS perpetual preferred, issued at about 90 versus a typical ~100 par, with roughly 15% yield and 18 months of dividends set aside, as an institutional-discount entry it expects to drift to par as retail arrives.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: New-issue Bitcoin preferreds can offer an institutional discount-to-par trade; watch for exits near par.

insights.claim: Anson underwrites the Strive preferred trade for about a 20% IRR over a short holding period (90 to 100 in roughly a month), saying it is not a fixed-income player and will mostly exit to retail near par, mirroring Morgan Stanley's original MicroStrategy deal.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Primary-issue discounts on perpetual preferreds are a repeatable arb; secondary buyers near par get yield only.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam says Strive trades at a multiple of NAV because it was set up by a legitimate, well-backed team, and was only the second treasury company to issue a perpetual preferred, following MicroStrategy (Saylor).
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Sponsor quality drives NAV premium among treasury companies.

insights.claim: Buyers of Bitcoin preferreds are modeling Bitcoin up 30–50% over the next year, which gives these instruments convexity beyond their coupon, per Moaz Kassam.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Bitcoin-preferred demand depends on bullish BTC assumptions; a BTC drawdown would hit the flywheel.

themes.theme: AI valuations and trading the LLM crowd

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam believes AI disruption is completely real but compares current valuations to the dot-com boom, questioning whether any company in the second or third inning should be worth $2 trillion when the eventual winner may come out of nowhere.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Underweight concentrated AI-winner bets; prefer structured deals around momentum over outright picks.
insights.quote: should a company in the second third inning of where the technology is heading be worth $2 trillion

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam flags the circular, interrelated financing among Nvidia, data centers and chipmakers as 'weirdness' in the AI ecosystem that makes him reluctant to take big directional bets.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Vendor-financing loops in AI capex are a fragility to monitor.

insights.claim: Private-market access to OpenAI and similar companies is a 'wild west' of layered SPVs charging fees on fees; Moaz Kassam says about 95% of people claiming ownership are not on the cap table, and sees stress building there, while noting Anthropic has been more prudent.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Avoid secondary SPV exposure to hot AI privates; layered structures signal froth and potential stress.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam says investors now drop short and long reports into Claude or ChatGPT and trade on the summary; Anson reads those AI summaries and finds about 75% of the time they miss something and 10–15% of the time they get it completely wrong, then trades against the resulting reaction.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: LLM-driven herd reactions to research reports create exploitable mispricings in momentum names.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam thinks his job and returns will improve because of AI, since other market participants are effectively becoming robots following another instruction.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Homogenized AI-assisted decision making increases crowding and reflexive errors for contrarians to exploit.
insights.quote: everyone else is becoming effectively a robot

themes.theme: Contrarian rotation: Korea memory, CoreWeave, Moderna

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam calls Korea the engine of the AI trade because Samsung and SK Hynix control memory, and says Samsung's last quarter was the largest earnings in history while many still think of it as a TV maker.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Korean memory makers are the leveraged earnings play on AI; consensus perception still lags.
insights.quote: Korea is literally the engine around this whole trade

insights.claim: After an AI selloff where everyone threw in the towel, Anson is going back into Korean memory names, expecting a 10–15% bounce within days or weeks as things stabilize rather than playing the long-term game.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Capitulation in memory stocks is a tactical long; expect a quick re-rate, then exit.

insights.claim: Anthony Pompliano notes the S&P 500 was only about 2% off its all-time high when the prior Friday saw the second-largest put buying in history (third-largest on the Nasdaq), arguing a non-decline would force covering and a rally.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Record put buying near highs is a contrarian bullish signal via forced hedge unwinds.

insights.claim: Anson bought CoreWeave the day Citadel told them they had never seen so much put buying in it, then sold after it ripped when everyone wanted back in.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Extreme put buying in AI infrastructure names has marked tradeable bottoms.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam is bearish on Moderna after a roughly 100% run on perceptions it has cured cancer, expecting a sell-the-news move before or around the trial efficacy readout due within about 10 days, as momentum traders exit early to avoid the binary event.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Short or avoid Moderna into the cancer-trial readout; momentum sellers may front-run the binary.
insights.quote: buy on rumor, you know, sell on news

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam says emotional retail belief about curing cancer is distorting Moderna's price, while experienced biotech managers are already burned and won't short, leaving few institutional holders.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Emotion-driven retail positioning without institutional support raises downside on disappointment.

themes.theme: Small-cap edge, long activism and SPACs

insights.claim: Anson avoids crowded mega-cap situations like a SpaceX–Tesla merger arb because large funds have better networks there, and instead targets smaller companies (roughly $100 million+ market cap, $4–5 million minimum positions) that big funds' size screens exclude.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Edge lives below institutional liquidity screens ($5–10B cap, $100M/day volume).

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam says almost no managers actually short single names for alpha anymore — they buy puts or short baskets — because of the perennial bull market and post-COVID volatility, and Anson has pivoted away from single-name shorting.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Scarce single-name short capital may leave overvalued names unchecked longer.

insights.claim: Anson started a long-activism group targeting companies of about $1 billion market cap and below, where fragmented retail ownership lets it take larger stakes and push buybacks, divestitures or sales, applying Elliott/Starboard-style playbooks at small scale.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Watch for Anson activist stakes as catalysts in sub-$1B names.

insights.claim: Anson is running an activist campaign at Lionsgate, arguing that amid media consolidation and the shift to streamers a proper sale process would value the company well above its current price.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Lionsgate is a potential takeout candidate with an activist pushing for a sale.

insights.claim: Anson has had activist success in Canadian REITs and Clear Channel in the US, zagging into real estate when sentiment was terrible.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Out-of-favor REITs remain activist hunting grounds.

insights.claim: SPACs have fallen back to trading near their trust value as small-cap momentum names (Russell, IWM) dropped 20–25% while the S&P stayed near highs; Anson is nibbling at SPACs with strong sponsors like Michael Klein, levering them since downside is limited to trust.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: SPACs at trust are a low-downside, levered option on sponsor quality and risk-on return.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam says space is a real long-term theme but investors are extrapolating too early; it lacks a daily news flow and is too speculative and long-dated to hold more than a small position.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Keep space exposure small despite SpaceX IPO enthusiasm.

themes.theme: Alternative data: prediction markets and social sentiment

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam considers prediction markets incredibly accurate — better than polling — because bettors often have real (even insider-like) information, and Anson uses them as one input in its investment calculus without trading on them directly.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Use prediction-market odds as an alt-data input for earnings and events.

insights.claim: Anson uses software to track positive versus negative retail chatter on names and acts on divergences and trend turns, rather than publishing on social media itself.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Social-sentiment divergence is a timing signal for retail-driven momentum names.

insights.claim: Anson monitors overnight and pre-market trading (including 24/7 venues and pre-IPO names like SpaceX and SK Hynix) where thin, margin-heavy liquidity lets stop-loss cascades drop prices 10–15% in an hour, which it buys.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Extended-hours liquidity gaps create discretionary buying opportunities.

insights.claim: Moaz Kassam describes funds like his as the casino relative to retail: retail believes it has an information edge but on average leaves worse off as funds exploit euphoria.
insights.speaker: Moaz Kassam
insights.so_what: Democratized trading increases exploitable euphoria for disciplined funds.
